title: Lake Malawi megadroughts
summary: Sediment cores from Lake Malawi record periods of severe aridity between 135 and 75 thousand years ago, when the lake's water volume fell by at least 95 percent. In the driest phase the lake, now about 706 m deep, shrank to a saline, alkaline body of roughly 125 m. After about 70 thousand years ago the climate became wetter and more stable across much of tropical Africa.

uncertainty.note: Scholz et al. give 135-75 kyr; Cohen et al. give discrete episodes 135-90 ka, with aridity easing after 95 ka. Years are before present counted back from the present.

importance.justification: Cores show tropical Africa was far drier than at the last glacial maximum for tens of thousands of years.
